senses.gloss:
अम्नस् ind. Ved. (स् being
changed to र् by P. VIII. 2. 70)
1
[]
Unawares, quickly.
--2 At present.
--3 A little.

आम्ना {c1c} P.
1 (a) To hand down
traditionally or in sacred texts;
भवत्प्रणीतमाचारमामनंति हि साधवः
Ku. 6. 31; एवं किल सूत्रकारा आमनंति
Māl. 7. (b) Hence, to regard, consider,
mention, lay down; त्वामामनंति प्रकृतिं
पुरुषार्थप्रवर्तिनीं Ku. 2. 13, 5. 81;
M. 1. 4; Bk. 18. 5; Kām. 8. 24; U. 5;
Mv. 4. 30.
--2 To keep in mind,
commit to memory, learn, study,
repeat; आमनन्मंत्रमुत्तमं Bk. 17. 30; यद्
ब्रह्म सम्यगाम्नातं Ku. 6. 16 learnt.
--3
To celebrate, hail.

आम्नात p. p.
1 Considered,
regarded, said to be; समौ हि शिष्टैराम्नातौ
वर्त्स्यंतावामयः स (शत्रुः) च Śi. 2. 10.
--2
Studied, repeated.
--3 Remembered,
[]
kept in mind.
--4 Handed down in
sacred texts or traditionally.
--तं
Study.

आम्नातिन् a. [आम्नात-इनि] One who
has studied the Vedas.

आम्नानं [आ-म्ना-भावे ल्युट्]
1
Recitation or study of the sacred texts or
Vedas.
--2 Mention; repetition in
general.

आम्नायः [आ-म्ना-घञ्]
1 (a) Sacred
tradition, sacred texts handed down
by tradition or repetition. (b) Hence,
the Veda, Vedas taken collectively
(including Brāhmaṇas, Upaniṣads
and Āraṇyakas also); अधीती
चतुर्ष्वाम्नायेषु Dk. 120; आम्नायवचनं
सत्यमित्ययं लोकसंग्रहः । आम्नायेभ्यः पुनर्वेदाः
प्रसृताः सर्वतोमुखाः ॥ Mb.
--2 A sacred
text or precept in general; U. 4.
--3
Traditional usage, family or
national customs.
--4 Received doctrine.
--5 Advice or instruction (in past
and present usage).
--6 A Tantra.
--7
A series of families.
--Comp.
--सारिन्
a. {1} pious, observing the traditional
usages. {2} containing the essence
of the Veda.
